This arrogant youth makes good that of Aristotle, who, differencing between age and youth, makes it a property ([ilegible].) of young men, to think they know all things, and to affirm lustily their own placits. He secretly insults over our Saviour ([ilegible]. 1.) as a triviall teacher, and calls for a lecture beyond the [ilegible], worthy therefore to have been sent to Anticyra: surely as when Drusus in his defence against a nimble Jesuite that called him [ilegible], alledged that [ilegible] must be in sundament is fidei, the [ilegible] replied that even that assertion was heresie: So when this young man affirmed that he had ever kept the Commandments, and asked what lack I yet? Christ might well have said, thou art therefore guilty of the breach of all the Commandments, because thou takest thy self to be keeper of all: and thou therefore lackest every thing, because thou thinkest thou lackest nothing.

entries.title: Matthew 19:21
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
As thou boastest and aimest: and which never yet any man was, nor can be here. The [ilegible] of this text made some of the Ancients count and call it consilium perfectionis, a counsell of perfection: such as whosoever did observe should do something more then the law required: and so merit for themselves an higher degree of glory in heaven then others had. Hence Bernard writeth, that this sentence of our Saviour filled the Monasteries with Monks, and the deserts with Anchorites.

Goe sell all, &c.] A personall command (for triall and discovery) as was that of God to Abraham, Go kill thy sonne [ilegible]. Christians may possesse; but yet as if they possessed not, they must [ilegible] loose to all outward things, and be ready to forgoe them, when called to loose them for Christ.

And give to the poor] So shalt thou clear thy self from all ([ilegible] quod ad pedes [ilegible]. [ilegible] to [ilegible].) suspition of coveteousnesse; which properly consists in pinching and saving: and so is distinguished by the Apostle from extortion, which stands [ilegible] immoderate getting, 1 Cor. 6 10. 1 Tim. 3. 3.

And [ilegible] have treasure in heaven] Far beyond the [ilegible] of Egypt, which yet is called Rahab, Psal. 89. 10. because of the riches power and pride thereof. Oh get a Patriarchs eie to see the wealth and worth of heaven: and then we shall soon make Moses his choice. In the year of grace 759, certain Persian [ilegible] fell into that madnesse, that they perswaded themselves ([ilegible].) and sundry others, that if they sold all they had, and gave it to the poor, and then afterwards threw themselves naked from off the walls into the river, they should presently be admitted into [ilegible]. [ilegible] hac insaniâ [ilegible], saith mine Author. [ilegible] cast away by this mad enterprize. How much better (if without superstition and opinion of merit) Amadeus Duke of [ilegible]) who [ilegible] asked by certain Embassadours that came to ([ilegible].) his court, what hounds he had, for they desired to see them? shewed them the [ilegible] day a pack of poor people feeding at his table, and said, these are the hounds wherewith I hunt after heaven.

entries.title: Matthew 19:22
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: That [ilegible] should require that, which he was not willing to perform. If heaven be to be had upon no other terms, Christ may keep his heaven to himself; hee'l have none. How many have we now [ilegible], that must be gainers by their religion, which must be another Diana to the [ilegible]. They are resolved howsoever to loose nothing, suffer nothing, but rather kick up all: Jeroboamo gravior [ilegible] regionis quam religionis. The King of Navarre told [ilegible], that in the cause of Religion he would launch no further into the sea, then he might be sure to return safe to the haven. A number of such Politick professours we have, that come to Christ (as this young man did) hastily, but depart heavily, when once it comes to a whole-sale of all for Christ, which yet is the first lesson, the removens prohibens.

entries.title: Matthew 19:23
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: With that burden of thick clay, that camels-bunch on his back: heaven is a stately ([ilegible] est opibus non [ilegible]. Et [ilegible] [ilegible]) pallace with a narrow portall; there must be both stripping and [ilegible], ere one can get through this strait gate. The greatest wealth is ordinarily tumoured up with the greatest swelth of rebellion against God. Vermis divitiarum est superbia, saith Augustine, Pride breeds in wealth, as the worm doth in the apple, and he is a great rich man indeed, and greater then his riches, that doth not think himself great, because he is rich. Charge those (1 Tim. 6. 17.) that are rich that they be not high-minded (for the devil will soon blow up such a blab in them, if they watch not) and that they trust not in uncertain riches, so as to make their gold their God, as all worldlings do, and worse: for could we but rip up such mens hearts we should finde written in them The God of this present world. They that minde earthly things have destruction for their [ilegible], Philip. 3. Have them we may and use them too, but minde them we may not, nor love them, 1 John 2. 15. that's spirituall [ilegible], such as Gods soul hateth, and he smiteth his hands at, [ilegible] 22. 13.

entries.title: Matthew 19:24
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Or, cable. rope, as some render it. Either serves; for it is a proverbiall speech, setting ([ilegible] [ilegible].) forth the difficulty of the thing. Difficile est, saith St Hierom, ut praesentibus bonis quis fruatur & futuris, ut [ilegible] ventrem [ilegible] mentem [ilegible], ut de [ilegible] ad delicias transeat, ut in coelo & in terrâ gloriosus appareat. Pope Adrian the sixth said that (Adrian [ilegible].) nothing befell him more unhappy in all his life, then that he had been head of the Church, and Monarch of the Christian commonwealth. When I first entered into orders, said another Pope, I ([ilegible].) had some good [ilegible] of my salvation; when I became a Cardinall, ([ilegible]. a Lap i. [ilegible] com. in Numb. 11. 11. [ilegible]. 1. [ilegible].) I doubted of it: but since I came to be Pope, I do even almost despair. And well he might, as long as he sate in that chair of pestilence, being that man of sinne, that sonne of perdition, 2 Thes. ([ilegible]. [ilegible].) 2. 3. Ad hunc statum venit Romana Ecclesia, said Petrus Aliacus long since, ut non esset dignareginisi per reprobos. The Popes, like the devils, are then thought to do well, when they cease to do (In [ilegible].) hurt, saith Johan. Sarisburiensis. They have had so much grace left we see (some of them howsoever,) as to acknowledge, that their good and their blood rose together, that honours changed their manners, and that they were the worse men for their great wealth: and that as Shimei seeking his servants lost himself; so they, by reaching after riches and honours, lost their souls. Let rich men often [ilegible] this terrible text, and take heed. Let them untwist their cables, that is, their heart, by humiliation, James 5. 1. & 1. 10. till it be made like small threeds as it must be, before they can enter into the eye of a needle, that is, eternall life.

entries.title: Matthew 19:25
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Because they knew that all men either are or would be rich; and that of rich man, scarce any but trusted in their riches. Therefore, though our Saviour told them, Mark. 10 24. that he meant it of those only that relied upon their riches, yet they remained as much unsatisfied as before, and held it an hard case that so many should misse of heaven. We have much ado to make men beleeve that the way is half so hard as Ministers make it.

entries.title: Matthew 19:26
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Because rich mens [ilegible] are ordinarily so wedded and wedged to the world, that ([ilegible]. 11. 41.) they will not be loosned, but by a powerfull touch from the hand ([ilegible] 2.) of heaven. Think not therefore, as many do, that there is no other hell but poverty, no better heaven then abundance. Of rich [ilegible] they say, What should such a man ail? The Irish ask, what they mean to die, &c. The gold ring and gay clothing carried it in St James his time. But he utterly [ilegible] ked [ilegible] partiality: and [ilegible] us that God hath chosen the poor in this world, rich in faith to be heirs of his kingdome; In which respect he bids the brother [ilegible] low degree, [ilegible] in that he is exalted in Christ.

But with God all things are possible] He can quickly root out confidence in the creature, and rivet rich men to himself. He can do more then he will: but whatsoever he willeth, that he doeth, without stop or hinderance. Men may want of their will for want of power. Nature may be interrupted in her course, as it was when the fire burnt not the three Worthies, the water drowned not Peter walking upon it, &c. Satan may be crossed and chained up: But who hath resisted the Almighty? who ever waxed fierce ([ilegible]. 9 4.) against God and prospered? Nature could say, All things are [ilegible] ([ilegible]. Linus Poeta.) to God, and nothing impossible: howbeit for a finite creature to beleeve the infinite Attributes of God, he is not able to do it throughly, without supernaturall grace.

entries.title: Matthew 19:27
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: A great All sure, a few broken boats, nets, houshold stuffe: and Christ maintained ([ilegible]. Pareus.) them too: and yet they ask, what shall we have? Neither is it without an emphasis, that they begin with a Behold. Behold we have forsaken all, as if Christ were therefore greatly beholden to them, and if the young man were promised treasure in heaven, doing so, and so, then they might challenge it, they might say with the Prodigall Give me the portion that pertains unto me.

entries.title: Matthew 19:28
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
As if our Saviour should have said, to forsake all is not enough [ilegible] ye be regenerate: So some sense it. Others by Regeneration understand the estate of the Gospel, called elswhere a new heaven, and a new earth, 2 Pet. 3. 13. the world to come, Heb. 2. 5. for God plants the heavens, and laies the foundation of the earth, that he may say to Zion, thou art my people. There are that understand by regeneration the generall resurrection (of which [ilegible] some think Plato had heard, and therefore held, that in the revolution of so many years men should be just in the same estate, wherein they were before.) These that follow this latter sense, read the text thus by an alteration of points, Ye which have followed me, shall, in the regeneration (when the Son of man shall sit in his glory) fit upon twelve thrones, &c.

Ye shall also sit upon twelve thrones] As so many Kings. Kings they are here but somewhat obscure ones, as Melchisedech was; but shall then appear with Christ in glory, far outshining (Colos. 3. 4.) the Sunne in his strength, higher then all the Kings of the earth. (Psal [ilegible]. 27.) When Daniel had [ilegible] the greatnesse and glory of all the four Monarchies of the world, at last he comes to speak of a Kingdome, which is the greatest and mightiest under the whole heaven, (Dan. 7. 18.) and that is the Kingdom of the Saints of the most high. So glorious is their estate even here: what [ilegible] it be then at that great day? And if the Saints (every of them) shall judge the Angells; What shall the Apostles do? surely as they [ilegible] or [ilegible] men in this world, so shall it fare with them at the generall Judgement.

entries.title: Matthew 19:29
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In reference to Isaacks hundred-fold increase of his seed. Gen. 26. 12. or that best of. grounds. Mat. 13, Those that do pillage us they do but husband us, sow for us, when they make long forrowes on our backs Psal. 126. and ride over our heads. Psal. 66, 12, Gordius the Mattyr said; It is to my losse, if you bate me any thing in my suffrings. Crudelitas vestra nostra gloria, said they in Tertullian, your cruelty is our glory: and the harder we are put to it, the greater shall be ([ilegible]. [ilegible].) our reward in heaven. Nay on earth too; the Saints shall have their losses for Christ recompensed, either in mony or monies-worth either in the same, or a better thing. Iob had all doubled to him, Valentinian, for his tribuneship, the Empire cast upon him, [ilegible] [ilegible] the Apostate, who had put him out of office, for his religion. (Qu pro Christi [ilegible] accepit [ilegible]. [ilegible].) Q. Elizabeth (whose life [ilegible] a long while had been like a ship in the midst of an Irish sea) after long restraint was exalted from misery to [ilegible], from a prisoner to a [ilegible]. Optanda nimirum est jactura quae lucro majore pensatur, saith Agricola. It is, [ilegible] a lovely losse, that is made up with so great gain. [ilegible] Q. Elizabeth forknown, whiles she was in prison, what a glorious raign she should have had for 44 years, she would never have wished her self a milk maid. So, did but the Saints understand what great things abide them both here and hereafter, they would bear any thing chearfully. An hundred [ilegible] here, and [ilegible] life hereafter: On who would not then turn spirituall purchaser? Well might St Paul say, godlines is profitable to all things. Well might the Psalmist say, In doing (in suffering) thy will, there is great reward. Not for doing it only, but in doing it: for Righteousnes is its own reward. St Mark hath it thus, He that leaveth house, brethren, sisters, father, &c. shall receive the same in kinde: house, brethren, [ilegible], father, &c. That is, 1. He shall have communion with God and his consolations, which are (Ne [ilegible]) better then them all; as [ilegible] that Italian Marquesse that left all for Christ avowed them: and as [ilegible], when his City was taken by the Barbarians, [ilegible] us to God, Lord let me not be troubled at the losse of my gold and silver, for thou art all in all unto me. 2. He many times gives his suffering servants here such supplies of their outward losses, in raising them up other friends and means, as [ilegible] abundantly countervail what they have parted with. Thus, though David was driven from his wife, and she was given to another, God gave him a friend Jonathan, (2 Sam. 1.) whose love was beyond the love of women. So though Naomi lost her husband and children; Boaz, [ilegible], and Obed became to her instead of all. The Apostles left their houses, and housholdstuffe to follow Christ: but then they had the houses of all godly people open to them and free for them: and happy was that Lydia, that could entertain them: so that having nothing, they (2 Cor. 6. 10.) yet possessed all things. They left a few friends, but they found [ilegible] more where ever they came. Wherefore it was a [ilegible] sarcasme of Iulian the Apostate, when reading this text, he jearingly demanded, whether they should have an hundred wives also, for that one they had parted with? 3. God commonly exalts his people to the contrary good to that evil they suffer for him: as Ioseph of a slave became a ruler: as Christ that was judged by men, is Judge of all men. The first thing that Caius did, after he came to the Empire, was to [ilegible] Agrippa, who had been imprisoned for wishing him Emperour. Constantine embraced Paphnutius, and kissed his lost eye. The King of Poland sent [ilegible] his enerall, who had lost his hand in his warres, a golden hand instead thereof. God is far more liberall to those that serve him, suffer for him. Can any son of Iesse doe for us as he can?

entries.title: Matthew 19:30
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Because Peter and the rest had called for their pay, (almost afore they had been at any pains for Chtist) he therefore quickeneth them in these words: bidding them bestir themselves better, left others, that are now hindermost, should get beyond them, and carry the crown. Lay (1 Tim. 6.) hold on eternall life, saith Paul: intimating that it is hanged on high as a garland, so that we must reach after it, strain to, it. So run that ye may obtain; Look you to your work, God will take care of your wages: you need never trouble your selves about that matter.

entries.title: Matthew 20:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
THat last sentence Christ further illustrateth and enforceth by this following parable. Peter and the rest were in danger to be puffed up with the preconceit of their abundant reward [ilegible], chap. 19 28, 29. This to prevent, and that they might not stand upon their tearms and tiptoes, they are again and again given to know, that [ilegible] that are first shall be last, and last first.

Which [ilegible] out early in the morning] God is found of them that seek him not, Isa 65. 1. Yea the Father seeketh such to worship him, Ioh. 4. 23. he solliciteth suitours and servants. A wonderfull condescension it is, that he looketh out of himself upon the Saints and Angels in heaven, Psal. 113. 6. How much more upon us poor earth-worms?

Labourers into his Vineyard.] Not loiterers. Iacob saw the Angels, some ascending, others descending, none standing still. God hath made [ilegible] to play in the waters, not so men: they must be doing, that will keep in with God.

entries.title: Matthew 20:2
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Not for eternall life, (for this those murmuring merit-mongers never had, who yet had their peny) but something (what ever it were) that gave the labourers good content: that it was for which each of them followed Christ, whether for meat perishing, or induring. (Job. 6. 27.)

entries.title: Matthew 20:3
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: For any good they did, or could doe, till sent into the vineyard, and set a work by God. Till then we are mere excrements of humane society. Nos numerus sumus, &c.

entries.title: Matthew 20:4
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: God hath his times to call men in: Only let them stand in Gods way, wait at the posts of wisdoms gates, at the pool of [ilegible], &c. [ilegible] & [ilegible] est adgratiam vocatio, Ephes. 1. 11. The separation of the Saints is wonderfull, Exod. 33. 16.

entries.title: Matthew 20:5
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: God hath his servants of all sexes and sizes, calling when and whom he pleaseth. And they have the comfort and credit of it that are first called, so they walk worthy of their time and that vocation wherewith they are called, Ephes. 3. 1. Thus it was an honour to Mnason, that he (Act. 21. 16.) was an old Disciple; and to [ilegible] and Junia, that Paul (Rom. 16 7.) should say of them, Who also were in Christ before [ilegible].

entries.title: Matthew 20:6
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: About five a clock in the afternoon. When it was well-nigh time to leave work. [ilegible] serò, si seriò. Howbeit delaies are dangerous, [ilegible] are abrupt, and headlong, and if once past, irrecoverable. If [ilegible] ye will enquire, enquire, [ilegible], [ilegible], Isa. 21. 12. [ilegible] that say, men may repent hereafter, say truly, but not safely. They that alledge these here that came in at the eleventh houre, [ilegible] consider that these were never called till then. But now God [ilegible], yea commandeth all men every where to repent, Act. 17. 30. And now he is more peremptory, [ilegible], then ever heretofore, See Heb. 2. 3. How many are daily taken away in their offers and eslayes, before they have prepared their hearts to cleave to God?

entries.title: Matthew 20:7
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: At this houre the [ilegible] was sent in, and he [ilegible] him: for he justifies Christ, condemns himself, chides his fellow for railing, praies for a part in Paradise, &c. he lived much in a little time. Howbeit [ilegible] is a singular example, one of the miracles wherewith Christ would honour the ignominy of his crosse. Neither is it often seen [ilegible] of, that old men are converted. They are usually so set in [ilegible] they are hardly removed: such an hoof they have over their hearts, that scarce any thing will affect them. Abraham in the old Testament, and Nicodemus in the New, were called in their [ilegible] age. Name a third he that can.

entries.title: Matthew 20:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: That is, to his Son Christ whom he hath made judge of all, to give unto every man according to his works. This he will doe with demonstration of his [ilegible] both justice (so that none shall receive lesse then was promised him) and mercy, (so that all shall receive more then they [ilegible].) For although their peny be here called their hire, [ilegible] elsewhere [ilegible] reward, yea their wages, yet all is of [ilegible].

entries.title: Matthew 20:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: These last [ilegible] were first [ilegible], because they trusted not to the worth of their own works, [ilegible] to Gods free grace and goodnes: when the other are turned off in displeasure, with Tolle quod tuum est & vade: Take thy peny and be packing.

entries.title: Matthew 20:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Good works are [ilegible] Regni caelestis, saith Bellarmine. But God is no such merchant. Caelum gratis non accipiam, I will not have heaven for nothing, saith Vega. Thou shalt never have it therefore; [ilegible] give thee that gift.

entries.title: Matthew 20:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: They had that they agreed for, some temporall blessings, which is all that carnall men commonly care for. Or if they seek after spirituall things, it is not for any beauty he seeth, or taste he findeth in them, but only as a bridge to bring them to heaven; as Spira confessed of himself. It is not good therefore to indent and bargain with God how much he shall give us, either of temporals or spirituals: for so you may have your peny, and yet be discontented, that it is [ilegible] a peny and no more. Profits, pleasures, honours, appear to be but empty things, when men are to goe into another world.

entries.title: Matthew 20:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Loe this is the guise of [ilegible] hypocrites to be quarrelling, and contending with God and man, as unworthily [ilegible] withall. Thus those Jewish [ilegible], Isa. 58. 3. hit God in the teeth with their good services, and small thanks. So the proud [ilegible] sets forth not his wants, but his worth. [ilegible], Jacob cries out in a low language, Domine non sum dignus, Gen. 30. 10. So doth Paul, 1 Cor. 15. 9. the Centurion, Matth. 8. 6. the Baptist, Mat. 3. 11. St August [ilegible], Non sum dignus, quem tu [ilegible], Domine, Lord, I am [ilegible] worthy of thy love.

entries.title: Matthew 20:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Friend he is called, not [ilegible], though he were a [ilegible], a merit-monger. In arguing the case with others, use hard arguments, but in a soft language; This will soonest work: for man is a crosle crabbed creature, and if roughly dealt with, will sooner slight you for your passion, then regard your reason, though never so convincing, because not well managed. There are a generation whose words (Rom. 3. 12. — 19.) are swords, whose tongues are rapiers to run men thorow with, (Psal. 17.) upon every small occasion, and their throats as a gaping grave to ([ilegible]. 17. 14.) bury them in.

entries.title: Matthew 20:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: A [ilegible] sentence. ([ilegible]. Imp. [ilegible] quantum est, [ilegible] est nisi [ilegible], quam di [ilegible]. [ilegible].) David blesseth himself from those men of Gods hand: which have their portion here, and that's all they are to look for. Valdè protest at us sum, said Luther when great [ilegible] were offered him, me nolle sic a Deo satiari. A gracious spirit [ilegible] rest satisfied with low things. The Turkish Empire, as big as it is, saith the same Luther, is nothing else but a crust of bread, which the good man of the house casteth to his dogs.

entries.title: Matthew 20:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
This is Gods speech (who is the great proprietary of all) it may not be ours who have nothing of our own, but all in trust: So that when we present any thing to God, we must say as David did, 1 Chron. 29. 14. and afterwards Justinian the Emperour, [ilegible] (Georg Cedren. Compend hist.) Of thine own we give thee: for all that is in the heaven and the earth is thine: St Bernard reports of Pope Eugenius, that meeting with a poor but honest Bishop, he secretly gave him [ilegible] jewels where with he might present him. If God did not first furnish us, we should have nothing wherewith to honour him, or doe good to others.

Is thine eye evil, because I am good?] It's commonly observed, that witches and those that are in league with the devil to doe mischief, are never given over so to doe, till they come to have an evileye. Hence that, nescio quis teneros, &c. and those that are ([ilegible], [ilegible] [ilegible].) bewitched, are said to be overseen, that is to be looked upon with an envious eye. Envy is a quick-sighted and sharp-fanged malignity, Prov. 27. 4. and doth, de aliena mente tam promptè quam pravè conjicere, as one saith, nimbly and naughtily guesse at another (Deg. Whear. Relect. Antelog p. 11.) mans meaning.

entries.title: Matthew 20:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
This is the purport of the preceding parable. Application is the life of preaching.

Few are chosen.] It's a strange speech of Chrysostom, in his fourth sermon to the people of Antioch, where he was much beloved, (Non arbitror inter Sacerdotes multes esse qui salvi [ilegible].) and did much good. How many, think you; shall be saved in this City? It will be an hard speech to you, but I will speak it: Though there be so many thousands of you, yet there cannot (Chrysost Hom. 3. in Act.) be found an hundred that shall be saved, and I doubt of them too: For what villany is there in youth? What sloth in old men? and so he goes on. See the notes on Mat. 7. 14.

entries.title: Matthew 20:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: To rouse them and raise them out of their carnall fears and dejections. Jerusalem was the (Revel. [ilegible]. 8.) [ilegible] slaughter house, Luk. 13. 33. (as Rome is now, which therefore is spiritually called Jerusalem, Egypt, Sodom, &c) Hither our Saviour bent his course: hereupon they were amazed and afraid, Mark. 10. 32. and gave him counsell to goe back rather into Galilee for his own and their safety, Joh. 11 8. He takes them therefore apart, and tells them as followeth, what they must trust to: and that though he be brought to the dust of death, he will rise again gloriously, to their great comfort.

entries.title: Matthew 20:18
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Behold, as it requires attention (and this was no more then need, for St Luke (Luk. 18. 34.) tells us that they understood none of these things, &c.) so it sets forth our Saviours forwardnesse, to goe this dangerous voyage.

entries.title: Matthew 20:19
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: What are all our sufferings to his? and yet we think our selves undone, if but toucht: and in setting forth our calamities, we adde, we multiply, we rise in our discourse, like him in the Poet. I am thrice ([ilegible]. [ilegible].) miserable, nay ten, twenty, an hundred, a thousand times unhappie. And yet all our sufferings are but as the [ilegible] and chips of that crosse, upon which Christ, nay many Christians have suffered. In the time of Adrian the Emperour, ten thousand Martyrs are said to have been crucified in the mount of Ararath, crowned with thorns, and thrust into the sides with sharp darts, after the example of the Lords passion. The chief of whom were Achaicus, (Act. and Mon.) Heliades, Theodorus, Carcerius, &c.

entries.title: Matthew 20:20
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Then, most unseasonably when Christ had by the parable been teaching them humility, and now was discoursing of his death and passion, then came these sonnes of Zebedee to beg a principality in Christs imaginary earthly Monarchy. And this is not the first time of their so foul mistake, so unseasonable a suit to him, or strife among themselves. The leprosy was cured at once in Naaman: so is not [ilegible] in the Saints, but by degrees, and at times.

The mother of Zebedees children.] Set on by her two sonnes, who were ashamed to make the motion themselves, (but as good they might, for Christ knew all, and therefore directs his answer to them, Mark. 10. 35.) and she also was not well assured of the [ilegible] of her request, and therefore came curtesying and craving a certain thing: not telling him what at first, as going somewhat against her conscience. And surely her request had been impudent, but that she presumed upon her neer alliance to Christ: For she is thought to have been sister to Ioseph, who was Pater Christi politicus: and thence her boldnesse, by reason of her right of kindred by the Fathers side. And this is some kinde of carnall excuse; Yet not for her and her sons foliy and vanity, in dreaming of an earthly kingdom, and therein a distribution of honours and offices, as in Davids and Solomons daies.

entries.title: Matthew 20:21
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
We may not over-hastily ingage our selves by promise of this or that to our best friends, but hold off and deliberate. Alioqui saliens antequam videat, cafurus (Bern.) est [ilegible] debeat.

The one on thy right hand] Quid voveat dulci nutricula [ilegible] (Horat.) alumno? Our Saviour had promised in the former chapter that the twelve should sit upon twelve thrones, &c. These mens suit was for the first and second seat. Self-love makes men ambitious, and [ilegible] them to turn the glasse to see themselves bigger, others lesser then they are, Paul on the contrary, was least of Saints, [ilegible] of Apostles.

entries.title: Matthew 20:22
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Ye ask and misse, because (Jam 4. 1.) ye ask [ilegible]. A prayer for things not lawfull, begs nothing but a deniall, as Moses did, in praying to enter into the land, Deut. 3. 25. as Job did in that peevish request of his that God would (Job 6. 8, 9.) let loose his hand and cut him off; as the Disciples did in that over-curious enquiry, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore the Kingdome (Act. 1. 6, 7, 8.) to Israel? Our Saviour answers, that that's not fit for them to know. But a better thing he could tell them, that they should shortly after be clothed which the holy Ghost. God sometimes in much mercy crosseth the prayers of his poople, as he did Davids for the childes life, who if he had lived, would have been but a standing monument of Davids shame. Was it not better for him to have a Solomon? The Saints have their praiers out, either in money or moneys-worth: provided they bring lawfull petitions and honest hearts.

Are ye able to drink of the cup, &c.] Afflictions are frequently set forth by this metaphor of a cup, taken say some, from an ancient custom that the father of the family should give to each under his charge a cup fit for his use, according to his bignesse: Or, as others think, from the manner of feasts, whereat the Symposiarch, or ruler of the feast, as he is called, Ioh. 2. prescribed what and how much every man should drink.

And to be baptized with the baptisme] Or plunged over head and ears in the deep waters of affliction. Of these we may [ilegible] as one doth of the Spa waters, that they are more wholesome then pleasant. Ever since Christ cast his crosse into them, as Moses did that tree, Exod. 15. 25. the property of them is altered, the waters healed.

They say unto him, we are able] In your own conceit at least, not else. For these two Disciples as they knew not what they asked, so they knew not what they answered. And yet Maldonat hath the face to defend them in it, as if they here [ilegible] their alacrity rather then betrayed their precipitancy: Sed exitus [ilegible] probavit: they shewed their valour at Christs apprehension.

entries.title: Matthew 20:23
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Illud solum quod [ilegible] est, & limpidius. The Saints sip of the top of Gods cup: as for the dregs, the wicked shall wring them out, and drink them up.

And be baptized, &c.] Or ducked, washed (not drowned) as St Paul was in the shipwrack; or as the baptized child, which shakes off the water, or is dryed after baptisme. Afflictions saith one, are called baptisme because they set Gods mark upon us (as baptisme doth) that we belong to God: This for outward afflictions. And for desertion, it is called Christs cup, because we are sure to pledge him in that too, and be conformed unto him, as was Iob, David, Heman, Psal. 88 &c. Grace is no target against affliction: but the best shall have terrours within, and troubles without, as sure as the coat is on their back, or the heart in their belly.

Is not mine to give] i.e. It is no part of my present office: Or, I have no such commission from my father to give precedencies to all that affect them. Christ hereby seeks to raise up the low groveling spirits of his Apostles to things supernaturall, supernall.

entries.title: Matthew 20:24
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: They were angry at that ambition in their fellows, that themselves were deeply guilty of. So Diogines trampled Platoes pride, but with greater pride. So Crassus earnestly inveighed against covetousnesse in others, when there was not a more covetous caitiffe then he upon the earth. So Gregory the great stomaked the title of universall Bishop to the Patriarch of Constantinople, which yet himself affected, and his successour Boniface arrogated and usurped.

entries.title: Matthew 20:25
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
We must (by Christs example) advance, cherish concord all we can, amongst ([ilegible] [ilegible] [ilegible] [ilegible].) ministers especially, by casting out those make-bates, emulation and ambition. Pareus was wont to say, that the onely cause of all Church-dissensions was, Ministers reaching after rule and preheminence, as did Diotrephes. And that if this evil humour could possibly be purged [ilegible], there would be a sweet symmetrie, an happy [ilegible] of all hearts.

And they that are great] The Grandees of the earth. There is, saith one, a greatnesse Belluine and Genuine. In that, a beast may and doth exceed us: In this we exceed ourselves and others. Great men are not alwaies wise, saith Elihu, Iob 32. 9. And [ilegible] me major nisi qui justior, said Agesilaus, when the King of Persia [ilegible] himself the great King. Calamitas nostra magnus est, said Mimus concerning Pompey, the people applauding so [ilegible] a [ilegible]. Privilegium unius conceditur in [ilegible] alterius, saith a learned Doctour: & si vis esse verè [ilegible], ne sis instar utris [ilegible] tumidi, sed instar uteri prole gravidi; [ilegible] attollas inane supercilium, sed exhibeas utile ministerium. Goodnesse is the only greatnesse.

entries.title: Matthew 20:26
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: How expresse is that against Papal primacy and Lordly prelacy? When the Duke shall be damned, what will become of the Bishop, said the clown to the bishop of Cullen? Mr Whithead refused a Bishoprick because he liked not to be Lorded. And Mr Coverdale being deprived of his Bishoprick in Q. Maries daies, would not (for the same cause) be reinvested in Q. Elizabeths, but taught a school.

entries.title: Matthew 20:27
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: This is the ready way to rise. Neither may any think himself too good to serve the Saints, to wash their feet, to minister to their necessities. Christ came out of the bosome of his Father to fetch them to heaven. The holy Ghost disdains not to dwell in their hearts. Angels are desirous to do them any good office. Prophets think not much to minister to them, 1 Pet. 1. 12. Paul and Apollo and Cephas are theirs, publike servants to the Church; accounting it a far greater matter prodesse quàm praeesse, to seek mens salvation, then to exercise dominion.

entries.title: Matthew 20:28
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: A redemptory, a valuable rate, for it was the blood of God wherewith the Church ([ilegible].) was purchased, Acts 20. 28. silver and gold could not do it, 1 Pet. 1. 18, 19. nor any thing else but that counter-price given by ([ilegible].) Christ, 1 Tim. 2. 6.

entries.title: Matthew 20:29
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Christ cured ([ilegible] in his locis [ilegible] curatos esse crediderim. [ilegible].) one blinde man as he went into Iericho, Luk. 18. and two as he went out; for all the haste he had to go to Ierusalem. Hence such multitudes followed him, to make up his ensuing triumph.

entries.title: Matthew 20:30
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Happy it was for them that, though blind, yet they were not d eaf. For as death came in by the ear, so doth life. Hear and your souls shall live Isa 55. 3. a heavy ear is a singular judgement, Isa. 6. 10. a [ilegible] ear a speciall favour, Prov. 20. 12. when God strook Zaechary, [ilegible]. 1. he made him dumb, but not deaf. When God strook Saul, he made him blind, but not deaf. When God strook Mephibosheth he made him lame, but not deaf. There is a deaf (Mark 9 25.) devil, and a deaf adder, and deaf man, that yet want for no ears, (I sal. [ilegible]. 4.) Isa. 43, 8. But he that heareth instruction is in the way of life, saith Solomon. These two blind beggers had heard of Christ by the hearing of the ear, but that satisfied them not, unlesse their eyes also might see him, Iob 42. 5. They way-lay therefore the Lord of light, who gives them upon their suit, both sight and light, irradiates both organ and object, cures them of their both outward and inward [ilegible] at once.

Thou son of David] They knew and acknowledged Christ to be the true Messias. Few such knowing blind beggers now [ilegible]. They are commonly more blinde in minde then body, loose and [ilegible]; such as are neither of any Church, nor common-wealth: but as the baser sort of people in Swethland, who do alwaies break the Sabbath, saying that 'tis only for gentlemen to sanctifie it: Or rather as the poor Brasilians, who are said to be sine rege, lege, fide, without any government, law, or Religion.

entries.title: Matthew 20:31
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In prayer, we must look to meet with many rubs, and [ilegible]; but Gods spirit is heroike, and gets over them all. The [ilegible] will interrupt us, as the [ilegible] did Paul, Act. 16. 16. as the birds did [ilegible], Gen. 15. 11. as those Samaritans did the Jews in building the Temple, Nehem. 6. Hence we are bid Strive in prayer, Colos. 4. 2. and watch in prayer: for Satan will be at our right hand as at Iehoshuahs, Zach. 3. 1. watching his time to cast in, if not a [ilegible], yet an impertinent thought, thereby to bereave us of the benefit of our prayers: besides our own naturall indevotion through hardnesse of heart, heavinesse of body, multiplicity of worldly distractions and [ilegible]. All which we must break through and cry the more earnestly as Bartimaeus here did, though checkt by the multitude. Have mercy on us, o Lord, &c. Daniel would not be kept from his God for any danger of death, ([ilegible].) [ilegible] [ilegible] 6: nor the French Protestants restrain prayer, though King Henry 3. made a law to forbid them to pray with their families. The sun shall sooner stand still then the trade of godlinesse, and that continuall intercourse that is betwixt God, and the Christian soul.

entries.title: Matthew 20:32
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: See the admirable power of fervent prayer. Christ stands and [ilegible] (for all the haste of his journey to Ierusalem, which till he had finished, oh how was he (Preces [ilegible] inantem remorantur.) [ilegible] Luk. 12. 50?) to hear the blinde beggers petition. So the sun once stood still in Gibeon, and the moon in the vally of [ilegible] upon the prayer of worthy Ioshua, who set the trophies of [ilegible] victorie in the very orbs of heaven.

entries.title: Matthew 20:33
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Truely the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun, [ilegible]. 11. 7, And yet how little is this mercy [ilegible], because common. Our corrupt natures heed nothing that we enjoy, as the eye seeth nothing that lies on it: but things at a distance it discerns clearly. Bona a tergo formosissima. Copy of good things breeds satiety, and makes them no dainties, till God for our folly many times makes us see the worth of them by the want of them, and so commends and indears his favours to us. But what a blindnesse is this, worse then that of Bartimeus, never to see the face, but the back only of benefits?

entries.title: Matthew 20:34
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
He made their case his own. Misericordia sounds as much as misery laid to (Isa. 63. 15.) heart. Christs bowels sounded upon the sight and suit of these blinde beggers: and this was beyond all almes, should he have done no more for them. For when one gives an alms, he gives somewhat without himself, but by compassion we relieve another by somewhat within and from our selves, whiles we draw out [ilegible] (not our sheaf only) to the hungry, Isa. 58. 10.

And immediatly their eyes received sight] This is not every blinde mans happinesse, that yet prayes for sight. But there is a better eye-sight then that of the body, which if God vouchsafe to any in bodily blindenesse (as he did to that blinde boy of Glocester that had suffered imprisonment there for confessing the truth) it may be said to such surely as Bishop Hooper the Martyr did to ([ilegible]. and [ilegible]. sol. 1371.) him; Ah poor boy, God hath taken from thee thy outward sight, but hath given thee another much more precious, &c. The like favour God shewed to Didymus Alexandrinus, who, though blinde from his childhood, yet was not only an excellent Artist, but an able Divine; and wrot certain Commentaries on the Psalmes, ([ilegible] in [ilegible] vir. [ilegible].) and likewise on the Gospels; being now (saith Jerome, who relates it) above 83 years of age. Trithemius and Bozius report ([ilegible]. de [ilegible].) the like things, concerning one Nicasius de [ilegible] a dutch-man, who being struck blinde at three years old, became neverthelesse an excellent scholar, and skilfull in the laws, which he publikely ([ilegible]. [ilegible] lib. [ilegible]. [ilegible]. [ilegible].) professed at Collen. Afterwards he proceeded Master of Arts at Lovain, Licentiate in Divinity at the same Vniversity, and lastly Doctour of the laws at Cullen: where, after he had printed his publike Lectures, he died and was buried in the Cathedrall-Church Anno Dom. 1491. 17. Calend. Septem.

entries.title: Matthew 21:1
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: IN this one verse, our Evangelist closely comprizeth all that St John sets down of our Saviours oracles and miracles from his seventh chapter to chap. 12. 12. viz. the history of five moneths and ten daies: for Christ rode not into the city till the fifth day before his last Passeover, Joh. 12. 12. having the day before been [ilegible] by Mary at Bethany, Joh. 12. 1. called here Bethpage, ([ilegible] a [ilegible] & [ilegible].) or the Conduit-house.

entries.content: There are that by the Asse understand the Jews laden with the Law: and by her foal, the Gentiles that wandred whither they would. That Canonist ([ilegible] & [ilegible] est. entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The Lord of all, both beasts and hearts: for else how could he so soon have obtained the Asse, of her master? Some read the text thus. The Lord hath [ilegible] of them, and [ilegible] presently send them back [ilegible]: to teach us to be no further burdensome or beholden to others, then needs must.

entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Here is the mystery of the history: which would otherwise seem to some ridiculous and [ilegible] little purpose. He hereby declared himself that King of his Church forepromised by the Prophets, how poor and despicable [ilegible], as the world accounts it.

entries.content:
Here was that also of the Psalmist fulfilled, God is my King of old working salvation in the midst of the earth, Psal. 74. 12. For Jerusalem is by the Fathers observed to stand in the very center and navell of the habitable earth, as if it were fatally founded to be the city of the great King.

Thy King cometh unto thee] All in Christ is for our behoof [ilegible] benefit, 1 Cor. 1. 30. & Micah 4. 8, 9. Unto thee shall it come, [ilegible] daughter of Zion, even the [ilegible] dominion: the kingdom shall come to thee daughter of Jerusalem. Why then dost thou cry out aloud? Is there no King in thee? Is thy counsellour [ilegible]? A Mandamus from this King, will do it at any time, Psal. [ilegible]. 4.

Meek, and [ilegible] upon an Asse] Not upon a stately palfrey, as Alexander, Julius Caesar, &c. no such state here. Christ Kingdom was of another world: He came riding meek, and his word (the law of his kingdom) is both to be taught and received with [ilegible], 2 Tim. 2. 25. Jam. 1. 21. At Genua in Italy they shew the tail of the Asse our Saviour rod on for [ilegible] holy relique; and ([ilegible]. [ilegible]. [ilegible]) bow before it with great devotion. Teaching us to honour God with the best of our substance, and to [ilegible] our selves wholly to the Lord our God. [ilegible] stripped himself, for his friend David, of the robe that was upon him and his [ilegible], (1 [ilegible]. 18. 4.) even to his sword and his girdle. Deum siquis parum [ilegible], valdè contemnit. And, one thing, said Luther, that will be the ([ilegible] in [ilegible], & [ilegible] tran [ilegible]. Luth.) entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Bondinus saith, he was met at this time by three-hundred-thousand Jews, some whereof went afore Christ, some followed after, according to the solemn rites and reverence used to be given to earthly Kings, in their most pompous triumphes. This was the Lords own work.

entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: So they acknowledg Christ to be the true Messiah, and congratulate him his kingdom over the Church; and yet a few-daies after, these same, at the instigation of the Priests and Pharisees, cry [ilegible]: dealing by Christ as Xerxes did by his steersman, whom he crowned in the morning, and then took off his head in the afternoon of the same day: or as the fickle Israelites dealt by David, 2 Sam 20. where we shall finde the same hands that erewhile fought for David to be all theirs, do now fight against him under the son of [ilegible], to be none of theirs.

Many live and dye very [ilegible], [ilegible] in [ilegible] places where they have had line [ilegible] line, precept upon [ilegible], &c. and yet they are no wiser then the child new weaned from the breast, Isa. 29. 8. their wits serve them not in spiritualls, though otherwise shrewd enough.

entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The Archprophet they acknowledge him; but of Nazareth, of Galilee. They had not profited [ilegible] much, or made so far [ilegible] in the mystery of Christ as to know him to have [ilegible] born a [ilegible]. And to nourish this errour in the people it was, that the devil, that old Impostour, Mark. 1. 24. though he confessed Christ to be the Holy [ilegible] of [ilegible], yet he calleth [ilegible] Jesus of Nazareth. Satan [ilegible] semèl videatur verax, [ilegible] est mendax & semper fallax. Satan [ilegible] speaks truth, but with a minde to deceave.

entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
The zeal of Gods house did ever eat him up. And (as revenge [ilegible] zeal 2 Cor. ([ilegible] [ilegible] [ilegible] [ilegible] [ilegible].) 7. 11.) he marrs their markets, and drives them [ilegible] of the [ilegible] with Procul ò procul este [ilegible]. The tables of the mony-changers] This he did also at his first [ilegible] into the ministry, Ioh. 2. 14. 15. See my notes on that [ilegible]. The [ilegible] of Religion was Christs chief care, and so it should be ours: And although little was done by his first attempt Ioh. 2. yet he tries again; [ilegible] should we; contributing what we [ilegible] to the work continually, by our prayers and utmost indeavours: ([ilegible]. entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
A principall piece of Gods [ilegible] worship, and [ilegible] put [ilegible] the whole. Christ [ilegible] never came into this house, but he preached [ilegible] as [ilegible]. In the Sanctuary was the incense-Altar in the middle, a type of prayer, the table of shew-bread on the oneside, [ilegible] the [ilegible] tribes; and the candlestick, a type of the word, on the other: To teach us that there is a necessity of both ordinances to all Gods [ilegible].

But ye have made it a den of theeves] So Christ calleth not the mony-marchants only, but the [ilegible] also that set them awork. And whereas they cryed, The Temple of the Lord, the Temple of the Lord (for to those was this speech first addressed, Ier. 7. 11.) as if they could not do amisse, because they served in the Temple, the Prophet tells them there, and our Saviour these here, that it's so much the worse. What should an Angel of darknesse do in heaven? Who required these things at your hands, to tread the courts of my Temple? This is the gate of the Lord, into (Psal. 118. [ilegible]0.) which the righteous only should enter. The Papists in like sort cry out at this day, Ecclesia, Ecclesia, Nos sumus Ecclesia: and herewith think to shrowd their base huckstering of holy things. For omniae Romae venalia, all things are saleable and soluble at Rome. But this covering is too short, and their grosse theeveries (Act. and Mon. fol 1[ilegible]84.) are now made apparent to all the world, as their rood of grace, and the blood of Hales were at Pauls crosse by that Noble Cromwell; and as their cheating trade of Indulgencies and Popespardons was by Luther, who by dint of argument overthrew those Romish mony-changers, and drove the countrey of those [ilegible] and [ilegible], as Nazianzen fitly calleth them.

entries.title: Matthew 21:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: So true was that testimony given of our Saviour, Luke 24. 19. that he was a Prophet mighty in deed, as well as in word, before God and all the people. Nos non eloquimur magna, sed vivimus, said the Primitive Christians. Our lives as well as our lips should speak us right and reall in Religion: As Christ here, by his cures, gave a reall answer to that question, ver. 10. Who is this? Let us learn to lead convincing lives: these are the best apologies when all's done.

entries.title: Matthew 21:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: To the great grief and regret of those cankerd carls the Priests and Scribes: but (Act. and Mon fol 866.) to the singular commendation of their parents, who had so well taught and tutoured them. So the children of Merindoll answered the Popish Bishop of Canaillon with such grace and gravity as was admirable. So, when John Lawrence was burnt at Colchester, (Act. and Mon. fol. 1403.) the young children came about him, and cryed in the audience of the persecutours, Lord strengthen thy servant, and keep thy promise.

entries.title: Matthew 21:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: [ilegible], thou hast given ([ilegible].) it all its parts, and proportions; thou hast compleated and accomplished it. The Hebrew saith, Fundasti, thou hast founded praise, and well bottomed it. Quae enim perfecta, sunt firmissima. Now there is no mouth so weak, into which God cannot put words of praise. But when he maketh inquisition for blouds (which he oft doth with great secrecy and severity) he [ilegible] such to purpos, Ps 9 12. as he did [ilegible], [ilegible], Charles the ninth of France, Felix of [ilegible], and sundry other bloudy [ilegible]. (Flac, [ilegible].)

Sent forth his Armies] The Roman spoilers, who were the rod in Gods hand, and revenged the quarrell of his Covenant: [ilegible] they thought not so, Isa. 10. 7. As in [ilegible] bloud by leeches, the Physitian seeks the health of his patient, the leech only the filling of his gorge: So when God turns the wicked upon his people, he hath excellent ends, howbeit they think not so, but (Isa. 10. 7.) to destroy and cut off nations not a few.

entries.title: Matthew 22:8
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Who were then? Such as came from the high waies and hedges, vers. 9. that is, such as sit and shew their sores to God, as the cripples and others do by the high-way-side to every passenger, to move pitty. Such sensible sinners shall walk with Christ in white, for they are worthy.

entries.title: Matthew 22:9
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Those sinners of the Gentiles, Gal 2. 15. who wandered in their own waies, Act. 14. 16. and were, till now, without God in the world, Ephes. 4. 18. These are those other husbandmen, to whom the housholder would let out his vineyard, chap. 21. 41, 43. which truth to illustrate this parable is purposely uttered, and principally as it may seem intended.

entries.title: Matthew 22:10
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Such a mixture there ever hath been, and will be here in the Church. Doeg sets his foot as far within the Sanctnary, as David. There are sacrificing [ilegible], Isa. 1. 10. sinners in Sion, Isa. 33. 14. We cannot avoid the company of those from whom we shall be sure to carry guilt or grief.

entries.title: Matthew 22:11
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
He is in the assemblies of his Saints to observe their carriage, and to adde measure unto them in blessing, as they do to him in preparation: he goes down into his garden to see whether the vinc flourish, and the pomgranats bud, Cant. 6. 11. he [ilegible] in the midst of the seven golden Candlesticks, &c. Now therefore we are all here present (Revel. 1.) before God, said [ilegible], Act. 10. 33.

Which had not [ilegible] a wedding garment] i. [ilegible]. Christ apprehended by faith, [ilegible] expressed in his vertues by holy life. Justification ([ilegible].) and sanctification are the righteousnesses of the Saints, wherewith arraied, they are beautifull even to admiration: as without (Revel. 19. 8.) the which, Satan stood at the right hand of [ilegible] the high Priest, because (as some will have it) his accusation was as true as vehement, so that Satan had the upper hand of him, tell such time as Christ bad, [ilegible] the [ilegible] garments from him; (Zech. 3. 1.) there he pardoned his sin in heaven: and unto him he said, Behold, I have [ilegible] iniquity to passe from [ilegible], and I will clothe [ilegible] with change of [ilegible], There he pardoned it, in his own conscience also.

entries.title: Matthew 22:12
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Not wretch, [ilegible], [ilegible]. Hard reproofs administred in soft language break the bones. See the Notes above on [ilegible]. 20. 13.

Not [ilegible] a [ilegible]] Is it fit to come to such a feast in thy worst? in the leathern coats, in the tottered rags and menstruous clouts of wretched old Adam?

And he was [ilegible]] He was muzzled or haltered up, that is, ([ilegible] Occlusum est illi os [ilegible] & freno ac [ilegible] animal [ilegible], ratione [ilegible]. [ilegible] in [ilegible].) he held his peace, as though he had a bridle or a halter in his mouth. This is the import of the Greek word here used. He was [ilegible], self-condemned, Tit. 3. 11. and could not [ilegible], chat [ilegible] God, Rom. 9. 20. as he used to do: he was gagg'd, [ilegible] it were.

entries.title: Matthew 22:13
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: He that comes in to Christs table without a wedding garment on his back, shall not go out without fetters on his feet. Neither shall it help him, that he hath eat and drunk in Christs presence. For his meat is sawced, and his drink spiced with that bitter wrath of God, Job [ilegible]. [ilegible]. He shall be taken as here, from the table to the tormenter. Look ([ilegible] Plut.) to it therefore, and come not hand over head. The very Heathens saw, and could say, That God was not to be served slightly or slubberingly, but with all possible preparation [ilegible]; hand.

entries.title: Matthew 22:14
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: With [ilegible] outward calling: but outward priviledges profit not, where the hidden man of the heart is not right, where the power and practice of [ilegible] is wanting. Many a ship hath been called Safe guard, and [ilegible], which yet hath split upon the rocks, or fallen into the [ilegible] of pirates.

entries.title: Matthew 22:15
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
They [ilegible], as one saith, [ilegible] & repuncti, minimè [ilegible] ad resipiscentiam compuncti. They were stung with the former parables, and grew more enraged. It is a [ilegible] perswasion for any godly man to think, by any discretion [ilegible] to still and escape the clamours and hates of wicked [ilegible]: Christ himself could not do it.

How they [ilegible] intangle him in his talk] As beasts are in the ([ilegible].) [ilegible] toil, or birds in the [ilegible] net. Every man hunteth ([ilegible]. Piscator. [ilegible]. à feris quibus [ilegible]. tur [ilegible] & [ilegible]. Par. [ilegible]. and Mon, sol. 1803. Ibid. 1116.) his brother with a net, was an old complaint, Mica. 7. 2. And, They [ilegible] a man an [ilegible] for a [ilegible], and lay a [ilegible] for [ilegible] that [ilegible] in the gate, &c. Isa. 29. 21. Doctour [ilegible] rule to know an [ilegible] was, They will say, The Lord, and, We praise God, and, The living God. So, The Lord, and not to say, [ilegible] Lord, is called by Steven Gardiner, Symbolum [ilegible], the heretikes badge. But God will take these wisards in their own craft, 1 Cor. 3. 19. he will catch them in their own [ilegible]. ([ilegible], [ilegible] & quasi [ilegible]. Aret.) he will over-shoot them in their own bow, he will take [ilegible] handfull of them, so that they shall not make escape, as the word there signifies.

entries.title: Matthew 22:16
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
i. e. Such as were of [ilegible] religion, as the Melchites, a kinde of mongrel-Christians in the (Nicephorus.) [ilegible]: so called of Melech, as one would say, Of the Kings [ilegible], because they followed the decrees and examples of the [ilegible]. Some thinke these [ilegible] were the same with the Publicans, or toll-takers (so Origen and Cyril) whom the Pharisees took with them to our Saviour, as if the one [ilegible] tribute, the other refused to pay, and both came to our Saviour, as to an impartiall Judge, to end the quarrell, and decide the controversie.

Master, we know that thou art true, &c.] Here's a fair glove, drawn upon a foul hand. Burning lips and a wicked heart [ilegible] like a potsheard covered with silver drosse, Prov. 26. 23: There are those that will smile in your face, and at same time cut your throat. Squier, sent out of Spain to poison Q. Elizabeth, [ilegible] the pummell of the Queens saddle with poison covertly, and as it ([ilegible]. 1598.) were, doing something [ilegible], praying with a loud voice, God: save the Queen, &c.

That thou art true, and teachest the way of God] These all are high commendations and necessary qualifications of a teacher and instructer of others. These Cony-catchers tell the truth of Christ (for he was all this that they say of him and more) and yet they tell a lie, because they thought him not so, but spoke against their consciences. They thought, belike, to have tickled and taken our Saviour with their flatteries (as every winde will blow up a bubble,) and so to have had what they would of him: But Christ was not for their turn. He was inadulabilis, unflatterable, and might better say then Politian did, Assentatiunculis quorundam, ant etiam obtrectationibus non magis attollor (Ang. Polit. epist. l. 3. ep. 24.) [ilegible] deprimor, quàm umbra mei corporis. I am no more lifted up, nor cast down with mens [ilegible] or slanders, then with the shadow of mine own body. For I think not my self [ilegible] longer [ilegible] shorter at morning, or at noon, because my shadow is so, &c.

entries.title: Matthew 22:17
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
They make it a case of conscience. [ilegible] sanctity is double iniquity. Covetousnesse goes cloaked or coloured, 1. Thess. 2. 5. So doth malice [ilegible] times: but God will wash off it's varnish with rivers of brimstone.

To give tribute] [ilegible], a kinde of coyn proper to this purpose. (Sands his Surv.) The Jews paid then to the [ilegible], as now they do to the Pope, and other Princes of Italy, a yearly [ilegible] for the very heads they wear. And yet how they brave it to our Saviour, and say, Joh. 8. 33. We were never in bondage to any man. And there is not (Alst. Chronol p. 432.) a more vain-glorious people this day under heaven, then the Jews, saith Alsted.

entries.title: Matthew 22:18
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Hypocrites pretend Nathaneel in the skin of a Nicodemus, saith one, of a [ilegible] rather, who made fair weather for a while, [ilegible] at length forsook Paul, and became an idolatrous Priest at Thessalonica, if Dorotheus may be believed. Jesus perceived these mens [ilegible], and detected it. So dealt Peter by [ilegible] Magus. whom Philip took for a very honest man, and baptised him. All will out at length; Quod sis esse velis, [ilegible] ([ilegible].) malis.

entries.title: Matthew 22:19
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Monachi pecunias attingere pro piaculo ducunt. No Cappucine among the Papists may take or touch silver. This mettall is as very [ilegible] to these, as the wedge of gold to Achan; at the [ilegible] whereof he starts back, as Moses from the Serpent. Yet he carries a boy with him that (D. Halls epist. [ilegible]. 1, ep. 5.) takes and carries it, and never complains of either mettall or measure.

entries.title: Matthew 22:20
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Not that he knew not whose it was, but that he might refell them by their own answers, judge them out of their own mouth; and that the people (into whose hatred they thought by [ilegible] captious question to draw him) might see that this was not more his, then the Pharisees own sentence.

entries.title: Matthew 22:21
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Not Give, but Render: As who should say, Ye give him but what belongs to him; ye doe him but right, ye helpe him but to his own, and that which he [ilegible] justly require of you, In [ilegible] patrocinij & [ilegible], in lieu of his care toward you.

And unto God the things that are Gods.] The Greek article is ([ilegible].) twice repeated, when he speaks of God more then when of [ilegible]; to shew, saith one, that our speciall care should be to give God his due. For if Caesar will take to himself Gods part, by [ilegible] that which is sinfull, to pay him such a tribute, [ilegible] tributum Caesaris, sed servitium diaboli, saith Chrysostom, It is not a paying of tribute to Caesar, but a doing service to the devil. [ilegible] non & animam nostram Dei imaginem soli [ilegible], ([ilegible]. Ens. Pandulf [ilegible] l. 5. [ilegible]. Neapol.) saith one. Let God only have our soul, sith it bears his [ilegible]. That was a witlesse and wicked speech of him, that said, [ilegible] he had two souls in one body, the one for God, if he pleased, the other (Ut eligeret ex [ilegible] tribus unū, vel [ilegible], vel [ilegible], vel perpetuum [ilegible]. &c. Hist. Gall) for any one else that would. But that was a gallant [ilegible] of the Prince of Condee, who being taken prisoner by Charles the ninth of France, and put to his choice whether he would go to Masse, or be put to death, or suffer perpetuall imprisonment? The former, said he, by Gods grace I will never do. [ilegible] for the two later, let the King do with me what he [ilegible], I hope, will turn all to the best.

entries.title: Matthew 22:22
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: With a flea in their ear, as we say. Confounded they were that they were so disappointed. Christ shaped them such an answer, as they could neither dislike nor digest. The [ilegible] mans eyes are in his head, but the fool walketh in [ilegible], [ilegible]. 2. 14. Ad [ilegible] properat, citò qui judicat. He that precipitates a [ilegible], shall soon see cause to repent him. How oft doth an open mouth prove a mans purgatory? We had great need therefore [ilegible] a pair of balances betwixt our lips, left we be entangled in our talk. For, Sis licet in partes [ilegible], Nemo tamen [ilegible], nemo cavere potest.

entries.title: Matthew 22:23
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: [ilegible] possunt [ilegible], [ilegible] tamen caudae in face eadem [ilegible]. Heretikes may differ as much from one another, as they all [ilegible] from the truth. Both Pharisees and Sadduces can conspire against Christ, though they cannot consent among themselves. These Sadduces were a brutish sect and sort of Jews, that held many [ilegible] opinions. Some of them are set down, Act 23. 8. Divers (Lib. 18. [ilegible] cap. 2. & de Bel Iud l. 2. c. 7.) other more grosse may be [ilegible] of in [ilegible], who also [ilegible] us, that they were but [ilegible] of them, yet of the chief among the people. And no wonder: for even at this day Atheists [ilegible] Epicures are rife; and among the great ones especially, who [ilegible] think or [ilegible] wish at least, there would be no resurrection, &c.

entries.title: Matthew 22:24
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
They pretend Scripture: so did the devil, Mat. 4. So do heretikes all; Sed sensum afferunt, [ilegible], but they fetch not the meaning from the Scripture, but [ilegible] a sense (even that of their own devising) on the Scripture: Cadem [ilegible] faciunt ad materiam [ilegible], saith [ilegible], They taw the text, as Shoemakers do their over-leathers, saith Polydor Virgil, that they may bring them to serve their [ilegible]: They lay the dead childe of their own corrupt glosses in the bosom of holy Scripture, and then cry out, It is hers, and not [ilegible].

If a man die, having no children] This Law these Sadduces ([ilegible].) [ilegible] to approve, when indeed they [ilegible] it, as the mother of much [ilegible] confusion, if there ever be a resurrection. So deals the devil and his Janizaries ([ilegible] I should say) at this day, by both Scriptures and Fathers, whom they [ilegible] or [ilegible], further then they serve their turn, to confirm their [ilegible].

[ilegible] up seed [ilegible]] Our children are a principall part of our selves, even the seed; as though now there were nothing left in us, but the chaff.

entries.title: Matthew 22:25
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Thus they that will marry shall have trouble, I, and that in the flesh, wherein they haply promised themselves most comfort and contentment. How many are there that seek an happinesse here: and, when to enjoy it might seem an happinesse indeed, they die, and [ilegible] all their thoughts perish. [ilegible] we have in Alexander the great, Iulius Caesar, Tamberlain, who making great preparation for the Conquest of the Turkish Empire, died of an ague in ([ilegible] hist s. 236) the middest of his great hope, and greatest power. The like might be shewed of many learned men, that died, when they might have been most usefull, as Keckerman, Perkins, Preston, Pemble, young Drusius, &c. All our learning is soon refuted with one black Theta, which understanding us not, [ilegible] us unrespectively without distinction, and putteth at once a period to our writing and to our being.

entries.title: Matthew 22:26
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Happy it was, if seeing their brethren [ilegible] so fast, themselves were warned to number their own daies, and provide for deaths coming. But this is not easily done; for we naturally dream of an immortality, Psal. 49. 11. and it is death to us to think of death, though we see so many daily die before us. It fareth with us for the most part, as with fatting Cattle. The Butcher comes to day, and fetcheth away one, to morrow and fetcheth away another, &c. The rest that are left behinde do neither mifse their fellows, nor dread their own destiny. So here, this is brutish stupidity, shake it off.

entries.title: Matthew 22:27
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: It is [ilegible] credible that one woman should out-live seven husbands. But grant she did, yet impartiall death, that had so oft-times cut [ilegible] her head, [ilegible] her heart at last. Death as an archer aiming at us, misseth us [ilegible], and hitteth haply some beyond us, some short of us, some on either hand of us; now our [ilegible], now our inferiours, now our equals, till at length we also are wounded; and the longer deaths hand is exercised, the more skilfull it grows. [ilegible] (Alsted Chronol.) de Temporibus, who is said to have lived in France above 300. years, died at length: So did the old, old, the very old man, Anno 1635.

entries.title: Matthew 22:29
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Ignorance is a breeder. All sins are seminally [ilegible] ignorance. S. Paul thanks it for all his (Arist [ilegible]. l. 3 Chem. [ilegible]. [ilegible]. [ilegible]. [ilegible]. 2.) [ilegible], 1 Tim. 1. 13. Aristole makes it the mother of all the [ilegible] in the world. All heresies, saith Chemnitius are known to have proceeded, Velex [ilegible] velex [ilegible] dialectica, velex AEtij [ilegible], from [ilegible], sophistry, or ignorance.

Nor the power of God] Who can as easily raise the dead, as he did at first create them. This the [ilegible] with all their learning, understood not: and therefore counted all that S. Paul could say to ([ilegible].) it bibble babble, because he preached Jesus, and Anastasis, or the resurrection, which they took to be some strange goddesse, Act. 17. 18, 19. They saw not how there could possibly be a regresse from a privation to an habit. Neither can any of us see it, [ilegible] God by his spirit of revelation, give us to know what is the exceeding greatnes of his power, according to the working of his mighty power, which he wrought in raising Christ, and us by him, Eph. 1. 19, 20. where it is easie to observe a six-fold gradation in the originall, and all to set forth the power of God, in Christs and our resurrection.

entries.title: Matthew 22:30
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Therefore our condition then shall be better then that of Adams in paradise, where he had need of a meet help, Chenegdo, such another as himself, a second-self. S. Luke adds the reason, why men shall not marry in the resurrection, viz. They can die no more; and therefore need not marry for propogation of their kinde, and immortalizing of their name. Mahomet, as he professed that himself had a speciall licence given him by God to know what women he would, and to put them away when he would: so he promised to all his votaries and adherents the like carnall (D. [ilegible] on of Gods Attrib. Blounts voiage, p. 67.) pleasures at the resurrection. Sensualists cast God and the things of God into a dishonourable mould: they rise not above their spring.

But are as the Angels of God] Are, that is certainly shall be; ([ilegible].) yea, in their head Christ they are so already. For God hath even here raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ [ilegible], Ephes. 2. 6. And at the resurrection, the just shall shine as the Sun in heaven, nay, as the Son of God himself, with whom they shall appear in glory, as his Spouse, Uxor (Phil. 3. ult.) fulget radiis mariti, is a maxime in law. Their vile bodies shall be conformed to his most glorious body, the standard in beauty, brightnesse, agility, immortality, &c. and other like unspeakable Angelicall qualities and perfections. Their [ilegible] shall be [ilegible] from all evil, fraught with all fulnesse both of grace and of glory.

entries.title: Matthew 22:31
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
In Moses, whose writings only they received, [ilegible] the rest. And the superstitious Jews at this day are said in [ilegible] to read two lessons, one out of the law, which is read by some chief person, another out of the Prophets, which is read by some boy or mean companion. For, savouring somewhat of these old Sadduces, they will in no sort do honour, neither attribute [ilegible] that authority to any [ilegible] of the Bible that they do to their [ilegible], which they do usually carry about their Synagogue ([ilegible] his surv.) at the end of the service in procession, with many ornaments of Crowns and Scepters; the children kissing it, as it passeth by them.

Spoken unto you by God It is God that speaketh in the holy Scriptures: It is the expresse minde of God that is there set forth unto us. See my True treasure, p. 10 &c.

entries.title: Matthew 22:32
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: That is, in the Sadduces sense, utterly dead and extinct for ever, but in S. Pauls sense, Rom. 14. 9. He is the God of the dead. For the dead bodies also of the faithfull, whiles they lie rotting in the grave, and resolved into dust, are united to Christ; by means whereof a substance is preserved, sinne only is [ilegible] with it's concomitant infirmities. But the rotting of the body is but to refine it: it is but as the rotting of corn under the earth, 1 Cor. 15. 36. that it may [ilegible] more glorious. Once, death to the Saints is neither totall, but of the body only; nor yet perpetuall, but for a time only. See both these together, Rom. 8. 10, 11. Further, from this verse we may learn, That there is a two fold knowledge to be gotten from holy Scriptures. 1. Expresse, I am the God of Abraham, &c. 2 By due deduction and firm inference, God is the God of the living.

entries.title: Matthew 22:33
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: This was well: But S. Luke adds, that which was more strange. 1. That certain of the Scribes said, Master, [ilegible] hast well said: No [ilegible] had (Luk. 20 39, 40.) ever so much ingenuity. 2. That the Sadduces were thenceforth [ilegible], and [ilegible] no more. [ilegible] her [ilegible] dare, quam turpitèr pugnare. Those Romish frogs the Jesuites will never have done, though never (Aristoph. in Ranis.) so much set down, but be still up with their hatefull Brekekekex. [ilegible]-coax.

entries.title: Matthew 22:34
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: Nunquam bella bonis, nunquam certamina de sunt. Truth never wants an adversary. Christ had many conflicts all his life long, but most and sharpest at last cast. At death, Satan will muster up all his forces against a Christian: that last encounter is like to be the sharpest; as Israel in the wildernesse met with much hardship, but when they entered the Land, all the Kings of Canaan combined against them.

entries.title: Matthew 22:35
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
Pareus gathereth (Ad liberandum igitur se [ilegible], partes disputan[ilegible]i adversus cum [ilegible] i uponi a [ilegible].) out of Mark, chap. 12. 28. that this Lawyer was one of them, that had applauded Christ for his conquest over the Sadduces in the last conflict, Luk. 20. 39. and that, for a penance he was enjoyned by his fellow-Pharisees, to undertake this following disputation with Christ.

Tempting him and saying] Saint Peter saith, They found no guile in his mouth, which implies that they sought it, 1 Pet. 2. 23. There are that hear us meerly to catch, cavill and quarrell.

entries.title: Matthew 22:36
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: The Rabbins reckoned up 613. Commandments of the Law: and distinguished them into the greater, and the lesser. These later they thought might be neglected or violated with little or no guilt. The Romish Pharisees have also their veniall sins, their peccadillo's, as we know; but the Scripture makes all sin mortall and destructory. A little strange fire might seem a small matter, yet it was such a sin, as made all Israel guilty, as appears by the sacrifices offered for that sin. Levit. 16.

entries.title: Matthew 22:37
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: God must be loved and honoured by us, [ilegible], saith one, truly, that there be no halting, and totally that there be no halving: he will not divide with the devil, as the Circassians are said to divide their whole life between rapine and religion. Gods service must be the totum hominis: Eccles. 12. 13. and the bonum hominis, Mic. 6. 8. We should (Brcer. Enq.) love him infinitely: which, because we cannot, we must love him unfeignedly: but how far short we come of loving him with all our heart, soul, strength, &c. (which yet the Papists affirm feisable) appears by our lives, which, do what we can, are fuller of sinnes, then the firmament is of starres, or the furnace of sparks.

entries.title: Matthew 22:38
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content: In respect of order, quantity and dignity. The second table is fulfilled in the first, and Luther is bold to say, Primo praecepto reliquorum omnium observantia praecipitur, In the first Commandment is commanded the keeping of all the rest. We rightly love our very selves no further then we love God: And for others, we are bound to love our friends in him, our foes for him.

entries.title: Matthew 22:39
entries.author: John Trapp (1601–1669)
entries.content:
For it hath, 1. The same author. God spake all these words. 2. The same tye. 3. The same sanction and punishment of the violation. 4. It requires the same kinde of love and service: for the love of our neighbour is the service of God.

Love thy neighbour as thy self] Now, thou lovest thy self truly, really, fervently, freely, constantly, hiding thine own defects and deformities as much as may be. Thou wouldst have others rejoyce with thee and condole with thee, as occasion serves. Go thou now, and do likewise to others. Howbeit our Saviour strains us up a peg higher, Ioh. 13. 34. His new commandment of the Gospel is, that we love one another, not only as we love our selves, but as he loved us. This forme hath something in it that is more expresse (in which respect partly it is called a new commandment,) and for the incomparable sufficiency of the president is matchlesse, and more full of incitation to fire affection.
